title: EA-CORPORA-13 — The Thirteenth Seating: The Alexander Seam (Plutarch's Alexander and Sulla; Arrian's Anabasis; Cicero's De finibus, Academica, Topica)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: Three corpora seated whole for the seam the Theophrastus line names next (The First Draft §28): the transition of the Aristotelian corpus from construction to spread by cultural conquest, and the grey space between Alexander and Rome. EA-CORPORA-13/01 Plutarch: the Alexander (Perseus tlg0007.tlg047) and the Sulla (tlg033) — chapter 7 of the Alexander transmits the esoteric/exoteric partition of the corpus as a letter: Alexander, crossing into Asia, writes that Aristotle did wrong to publish the acroamatic works (τίνι γὰρ δὴ διοίσομεν ἡμεῖς τῶν ἄλλων), and Aristotle apologizes that they are published and not published (ὡς καὶ ἐκδεδομένων καὶ μὴ ἐκδεδομένων); chapter 8 carries the Iliad ἐκ τοῦ νάρθηκος, chapter 55 Callisthenes; Sulla 26 the Rome hinge (Apellicon, Tyrannion, Andronicus). EA-CORPORA-13/02 Arrian, Anabasis Alexandri whole (tlg0074.tlg001): the administrative Alexander (I 17 Sardis; IV 10–14 Callisthenes), for the Macedonian dossier of §16. EA-CORPORA-13/03 Cicero, De finibus, Academica (book I as Perseus carries it; the Lucullus is a stub in the source and remains unseated), Topica (phi0474.phi048, phi045, phi054): the first Roman reader, who knows Aristotle by the dialogues and the exoterica and not by the treatises. Each seat carries originals, normalized text, source.json with verified loci, and a SHA-256 manifest; each renders as a card on traininglayerliterature.org; the index at data/api/corpora.json carries all three. Not seated, named as debts: the Alexander Romance (pseudo-Callisthenes — no open TEI located), the Rhetorica ad Alexandrum (not in First1KGreek), Cicero's Lucullus.

Fetched, normalized and seated in-session by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) at MANUS (Lee Sharks) direction from the Perseus canonical-greekLit and canonical-latinLit repositories; the identification of the seam and of the grey space is Lee Sharks's; the first reading of Alexander 7 is recorded in the notebook (§28) and belongs to the next standalone.

wiki_article: EA-CORPORA-13, the thirteenth seating of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive (7 September 2026), seats three corpora whole for the Alexander seam — the transition of the Aristotelian corpus from construction to spread by cultural conquest, and the grey space between Alexander and Rome: Plutarch's Alexander and Sulla, Arrian's Anabasis Alexandri, and Cicero's De finibus, Academica and Topica, each with originals, normalized text, verified loci and a SHA-256 manifest, indexed and rendered on the traininglayerliterature.org shelf. The seam's first text is Plutarch, Alexander 7, where the esoteric/exoteric partition of the corpus is transmitted as a letter: Alexander, crossing into Asia, complains that Aristotle published the acroamatic works — in what shall we excel the rest? — and Aristotle replies that they are published and not published. Named as debts: the Alexander Romance, the Rhetorica ad Alexandrum, Cicero's Lucullus.
